name.text: Transverse common tangent length - interactive circles (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
Two circles are shown below: the blue circle has centre \(A\) and radius \(r\); the red circle has centre \(B\) and radius \(R\). The two transverse common tangents (the ones that cross between the circles) are drawn, and the contact points of one of them are marked \(T\) and \(T'\). The length \(L = TT'\) is highlighted.

Drag the circles around — move the centres \(A\) and \(B\), and drag the small open points to change the radii. The box keeps \(r\), \(R\) and \(d = AB\) up to date for whatever arrangement you choose.

\( L = \) [[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Tip: drag the circles to a new position and the question changes — try a few and check you can get each one right. Remember the circles must be fully apart for a transverse tangent to exist.

generalfeedback.text:
For two circles with radii \(r\) and \(R\) whose centres are a distance \(d\) apart, the length of a transverse (inverse) common tangent is

\[ L = \sqrt{d^{2} - (R + r)^{2}}. \]

This comes from the right-angled triangle in which the line of centres \(AB\) is the hypotenuse (length \(d\)), the sum of the radii \(R+r\) is one leg, and the tangent length \(L = TT'\) is the other leg, so \(d^2 = L^2 + (R+r)^2\). The sum appears (rather than the difference, as for a direct tangent) because the circles sit on opposite sides of the tangent.

/*

You simply read \(r\), \(R\) and \(d\) from your diagram and substitute. For example, with \(r = {@ri@}\), \(R = {@Rr@}\) and \(d = {@d0@}\),

\[ L = \sqrt{ {@d0@}^{2} - ({@Rr@} + {@ri@})^{2} } = \sqrt{ {@d0^2 - (Rr+ri)^2@} } \approx {@fr(L0t)@}. \] */

questionnote.text: Start config: \( r={@ri@},\ R={@Rr@},\ d={@d0@},\ L\approx{@fr(L0t)@} \) (student may drag to change it)

truefeedback.text: In your current arrangement the circles are not fully apart (\(d \le R + r\)), so there is no transverse common tangent and \(L\) is not defined. Drag the circles apart (so that \(d > R + r\)) and try again.

node.description: Used R-r (direct formula) instead of R+r.

truefeedback.text: You have used \(R - r\). That is the direct common tangent formula. For a transverse common tangent the circles are on opposite sides of the tangent, so use the sum of the radii: \(L = \sqrt{d^{2} - (R + r)^{2}}\).

node.description: Linear subtraction d - (R+r) instead of Pythagoras.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you computed \(d - (R + r)\). The radii and the line of centres form a right-angled triangle, so you must use Pythagoras: \(L = \sqrt{d^{2} - (R + r)^{2}}\), not a straight subtraction.
That is \(d\), the distance between the centres. You still need to subtract \((R+r)^2\) and take the square root: \(L = \sqrt{d^{2} - (R + r)^{2}}\).

falsefeedback.text: Not correct for your circles. Read \(r\), \(R\) and \(d\) from the box and substitute into \(L = \sqrt{d^{2} - (R + r)^{2}}\). Remember to square, subtract, then take the square root.
